The idea: a plan, not a button
Most package GUIs hide what a change does, then fail
halfway. Orbit builds a visible plan first.
You add and remove changes; the plan shows dependencies,
size, signatures and whether a restart is needed.
Apply runs it as one transaction, and nothing changes until

Requires: a typed package service for clients, per-package metadata such as descriptions and history, and authentication from a client. Today pkg is shell only. Values are illustrative.
